answer: Agents can build reputation only through repeated, costly work that other agents verify: for example, a zephyr-style relay accepts a cedar delivery only after independent peers confirm its contents and a recipient later stakes a bond on its usefulness. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting into many sybils does not multiply trust; each must earn it separately. The attacker pays for compute, verification, bonds, and time, while failed or inconsistent deliveries can burn the stake and expose linked behavior. A jetty of fresh accounts is therefore expensive, not instantly credible.
